newsitem.title: THAILAND: Karen refugees flee Burma for Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Karen refugees flee Burma for Thailand.

text.p: About 16,000 Karen refugees streamed into Thailand on Thursday, a day after Burmese troops attacked key Karen National Union (KNU) guerrilla camps in Burma, Thai officials said.
Border Patrol Police sources based in Umphang district of Thailand's northern Take province told Reuters the refugees had scattered in the jungle.
On Wednesday, about 2,000 refugees were reported by the Thai army to have crossed over.
"They keep coming and I think the number will swell up to more than the 16,000 soon," a police source said on Thursday.
Burmese troops on Wednesday attacked three KNU mobile camps in Burma's eastern jungle with mortars and artillery and dispersed about 4,000 KNU guerrillas, Thai military sources said.
About 70,000 ethnic Karen refugees, who fled fighting inside Burma, have been living in sprawling refugee camps along Thailand's border for years.
The refugees are family members and followers of the KNU which has been fighting the Burmese military government for greater autonomy for the Karen state since Burmese independence in 1948.
A Burmese government spokesman declined to give details of the operation against the KNU rebels but said in a statement to Reuters that operations had begun before Wednesday.
"We do not regard these troop movements as an offensive...," he said. "The door for meaningful peace talks with the KNU is always open on the government's side."

KNU, a predominantly Christian group, used to be the strongest among a dozen ethnic minority rebel groups fighting Rangoon. It has refused to lay down its arms and has rejected peace overtures by the Burmese government.
But in 1995, the KNU suffered a major setback when Buddhist members of the group staged a mutiny, split from the mainstream and formed the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army.
The new faction, said to be backed by Rangoon, recently launched attacks against KNU camps and Karen refugees close to the Thai border.
A Thai military spokesman said the new stream of Karen refugees would be given humanitarian assistance.
"We will provide humanitarian assistance to the displaced persons who have fled problems in their country. But for those fighting, Thailand will not interfere in their internal affairs," he said.
Exiled Burmese students of the All Burma Students Democratic Front (ABSDF) condemned the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council's (SLORC) latest attack on the KNU camps.
"The ABSDF strongly condemns the SLORC's new offensive against the KNU...which has led to the breakdown of peace talks between the two parties," it said in a statement.
